I've already got the image, so now I'm pulling the key details from this Chinese delivery note out of Dongguan Precision Housings: number SN-261007-130, dated 2026-10-07, under PO 4500318715, with a line for 20 packages of 20,200 pieces of CMP-GAM-006 Steel Case Grand Heist 6, and 300 kg gross carried by Nordhav Shipping A/S.

I'm reading the quantity as 20,200 pieces rather than 20.2, since a piece count can't be fractional and the document uses a period as a thousands separator, though that's a judgment call I'll flag. The received stamp reads 10.11.2026 in German date order, which is 10 November 2026, about five weeks after the 7 October document date.

I'm checking the remaining fields now: the remark about objections within three days, and whether the stamp counts as an acceptance decision. It reads as a receipt acknowledgment rather than an inspection, so I'm leaving the decisions open. The red stamp partly covers the unit column and the PCS cell, but the unit is still readable, so I'm noting that as an observation. The values I'm recording are the printed quantity and packages, the 300 kg weight, the stamped received date, the document date, and the PO and delivery note numbers.

Packages are listed twice, in the table and in the footer count, so I'll record them once and keep the weight at 300 kg.
